action.action-desc: Mr. Scott of Virginia (for himself, Ms. Omar, and Mr. Casar) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce

form.official-title: To amend the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to prohibit the garnishment of wages in relation to medical debt, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Protecting Workers' Wages from Medical Debt Act.

section.header: Prohibition on wage garnishment for medical debts

subsection.text: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (29 U.S.C. 201 et seq.) is amended by inserting after section 7 the following:

section.header: Prohibition on wage garnishment for medical debts

subsection.text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no wages of an employee may be subject to garnishment for the payment of any medical debt.
No court of the United States or any State, and no State (or officer or agency thereof), may make, execute, or enforce any order or process in violation of this section.

paragraph.text: The term garnishment means any legal or equitable procedure through which the wages of any individual are required to be withheld for payment of any medical debt.

.The term medical debt means a debt arising from the furnishing of items and services by a health care facility or health care provider (as defined in section 101(6) of the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993 (29 U.S.C. 2611(6)).

subsection.text: Section 10 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (29 U.S.C. 210) is repealed.
This Act shall take effect on the date that is 6 months after the date of enactment of this Act.
